host.name: devbox_capabilities
host.description: Read the current Rust contract version, schema hash, tools and scheduling/admission limits. Supply a tool_name for its authoritative schema to diagnose cached connector definitions.

host.name: devbox_exec
host.title: Run Mutating Shell Command In Windows Host Devbox
host.description: Use this when the shell command needs side effects such as writing files, building artifacts, installing packages, changing git state, or otherwise mutating the Windows host devbox. Prefer devbox_run_program for a single executable and devbox_exec_readonly for shell-based inspection. Synchronous calls are capped at 90s; use devbox_exec_start for builds or other longer work.

command.description: Shell command to execute in the selected Devbox runtime.

host.name: devbox_exec_readonly
host.title: Run Read-Only Shell Command In Windows Host Devbox
host.description: Use this only when inspection requires shell syntax such as pipelines, redirection, variables, or compound commands. Prefer devbox_run_program for a single executable such as git, gh, node, python, or rg because it avoids shell startup overhead. In Windows host devbox mode this runs directly on the host shell, so read-only behavior is advisory rather than sandbox-enforced. Synchronous calls are capped at 90s; use devbox_exec_start for longer work.

command.description: Shell command to execute in the selected Devbox runtime.

host.name: devbox_exec_start
host.title: Start Background Shell Job In Windows Host Devbox
host.description: Use this for Windows host devbox commands expected to run longer than about 90 seconds. It starts a detached persisted job and returns immediately so connector request deadlines do not cancel the work.

command.description: Shell command to run as a detached Devbox job.

host.name: devbox_file_state
host.description: Read a complete file digest and length before an atomic checkpoint write. Host runtime only.

host.name: devbox_github_auth_status
host.title: Windows Host Devbox GitHub Auth Status
host.description: Use this when you need to confirm whether the Windows host devbox is authenticated to GitHub and which git identity is configured.

host.name: devbox_job_cancel
host.title: Cancel Devbox Background Job
host.description: Use this to stop a job started by devbox_exec_start. The detached runner and its process tree are terminated.

host.name: devbox_job_list
host.description: Discover persisted jobs with task/status filters and bounded job-ID pagination. Recover job IDs after reconnecting.

host.name: devbox_job_logs
host.title: Read Devbox Background Job Logs
host.description: Use this to retrieve bounded stdout/stderr tails for a job started by devbox_exec_start.

host.name: devbox_job_status
host.title: Get Devbox Background Job Status
host.description: Read background-job status. Prefer wait_seconds instead of Start-Sleep polling; waiting here uses only a Node timer and consumes no execution slot or shell process.

wait_seconds.description: Optional no-slot long-poll duration in seconds (0-85).

host.name: devbox_job_submit
host.description: Submit a durable host job using a task_id and operation_id. Exactly one of program or command is required. Retry the identical operation after response loss: it returns the existing job, never launches a duplicate. Conflicting reuse is rejected; admission limits bound queued runners.

host.name: devbox_list_files
host.title: List Windows Host Devbox Files
host.description: Use this when you need a directory listing inside the Windows host devbox workspace or another configured path.

host.name: devbox_read_file
host.title: Read Windows Host Devbox File
host.description: Use this when you need text content from a file inside the Windows host devbox.

host.name: devbox_read_large_file
host.title: Read Large Windows Host Devbox File Chunk
host.description: Use this when you need an exact byte range from a larger file inside the Windows host devbox. It returns a base64 chunk plus metadata for safe paging without UTF-8 corruption.

host.name: devbox_recreate
host.title: Recreate Windows Host Devbox
host.description: Use this when the Windows host devbox should be rebuilt from the configured backend while preserving the workspace.

host.name: devbox_restart
host.title: Restart Windows Host Devbox
host.description: Use this when the Windows host devbox needs a clean restart.

host.name: devbox_run_program
host.title: Run Program Directly In Windows Host Devbox
host.description: Preferred fast path for running one executable with structured arguments inside the Windows host devbox (for example git, gh, node, python, or rg). This avoids shell startup and quoting overhead. Use devbox_exec or devbox_exec_readonly only when shell syntax is actually required.

program.description: Executable name from DEVBOX_PROGRAM_ALLOWLIST; no shell syntax is interpreted.

args.description: Argument vector passed directly to the executable.

working_dir.description: Working directory; defaults to the selected Devbox workspace.

user.description: Execution user; primarily useful for Docker mode.

output_mode.description: Output shaping mode: head, tail, or summary.

max_output_chars.description: Maximum characters returned per output stream.

max_output_lines.description: Optional maximum lines returned per stream; 0 disables line limiting.

host.name: devbox_run_program_start
host.title: Start Background Program Directly In Windows Host Devbox
host.description: Preferred detached path for one long-running executable. It avoids shell startup/quoting and participates in weighted scheduling. Use resource_class=watch for passive watchers and heavy for builds/browser workloads.

program.description: Executable name from DEVBOX_PROGRAM_ALLOWLIST; no shell syntax is interpreted.

resource_class.description: Resource class: auto, watch, light, heavy, or io-heavy.

host.name: devbox_search_files
host.title: Search Windows Host Devbox Files
host.description: Use this when you need text search inside the Windows host devbox workspace. ripgrep-style syntax is supported best-effort in host mode.

host.name: devbox_start
host.title: Start Windows Host Devbox
host.description: Use this when the Windows host devbox is stopped or missing and needs to be brought online.

host.name: devbox_status
host.title: Windows Host Devbox Status
host.description: Use this when you need the current state of the Windows host devbox and its installed toolchain.

host.name: devbox_stop
host.title: Stop Windows Host Devbox
host.description: Use this when the Windows host devbox should be shut down without deleting the workspace.

host.name: devbox_sync_github_auth_from_host
host.title: Sync Host GitHub Auth Into Windows Host Devbox
host.description: Use this when the host already has a valid GitHub CLI login and the Windows host devbox should inherit GitHub authentication and git identity from the host.

host.name: devbox_task_get
host.description: Read a versioned task checkpoint, including plan, job IDs and artifact references saved by the agent.

host.name: devbox_task_list
host.description: Discover task IDs and revisions after reconnecting, without loading large task states.

host.name: devbox_task_put
host.description: Atomically save task state using expected_revision (zero creates a task). Stale updates are rejected; identical retries recover the committed revision. State is data and does not grant execution permissions.

host.name: devbox_wait
host.title: Wait Without Consuming An Execution Slot
host.description: Use this instead of Start-Sleep/sleep when you simply need to wait before the next MCP action. It uses a Node timer only: no PowerShell process and no execution slot.

seconds.description: How long to wait, in seconds.

host.name: devbox_wait_for_file
host.title: Wait For Host File Condition Without A Shell
host.description: Host-mode filesystem condition wait using Node fs polling only. Prefer this over Start-Sleep followed by Test-Path/Get-Content. Docker mode should use devbox_wait because container paths are not directly visible to the MCP process.

should_exist.description: Wait for the path to exist; false waits for removal.

min_bytes.description: When waiting for existence, require at least this file size.

stable_ms.description: Require the condition to remain true for this duration.

host.name: devbox_write_file
host.title: Write Windows Host Devbox File
host.description: Use this when you need to create or overwrite a text file inside the Windows host devbox workspace.

host.name: devbox_write_file_atomic
host.description: Atomically replace a host file after checking its previous SHA-256 (or missing). Append requires the previous offset; identical retries return replayed=true without duplicating bytes. Uses bounded-memory staging; atomic append copies the previous file.

expected_file_sha256.description: Previous complete file SHA-256, or "missing" for create-only.

expected_offset_bytes.description: Required for retry-safe append, measured before the first attempt.

host.name: devbox_write_large_file
host.title: Write Large Windows Host Devbox File
host.description: Use this when you need to create or overwrite a large file inside the Windows host devbox workspace using base64-backed transfer with post-write verification.

host.name: host_capture_display
host.title: Capture Windows Host Display
host.description: Capture the complete windows host desktop using the native compositor/screenshot backend and return an MCP image content block. Windows returns JPEG; macOS/Linux use lossless PNG when their native tools do.

quality.description: Requested image quality from 1 through 100. Native lossless PNG backends record but do not apply JPEG quality.

host.name: host_capture_program
host.title: Capture Windows Host Window by PID
host.description: Compatibility alias for host_capture_window.

pid.description: Host process ID whose visible application window should be captured.

include_process_tree.description: Also consider visible windows owned by child processes, useful for launchers, browsers, emulators, and multi-process GUI applications.

host.name: host_capture_window
host.title: Capture Windows Host Window by PID
host.description: Capture the largest visible window owned by a host PID or one of its child processes. The Windows backend detects black PrintWindow frames from GPU/DirectComposition surfaces and falls back to compositor-visible pixels. macOS uses CoreGraphics window discovery plus screencapture; Linux supports X11 and compositor-specific Wayland paths.

pid.description: Host process ID whose visible application window should be captured.

include_process_tree.description: Also consider visible windows owned by child processes, useful for launchers, browsers, emulators, and multi-process GUI applications.

host.name: host_exec
host.title: Run Windows PowerShell Command
host.description: Use this when you explicitly need native windows host shell automation rather than the Windows host devbox. Prefer host_run_program for a single allowed executable such as git, gh, node, python, or rg because it avoids PowerShell startup overhead. On Windows this runs elevated inside the already-elevated MCP service (no per-command UAC).

host.name: host_run_program
host.title: Run Allowed Windows Host Program
host.description: Preferred fast path when you need a specific allowed windows host program such as git, gh, node, python, or rg with structured arguments; this avoids shell startup and quoting overhead.

host.name: host_status
host.title: Windows Host Tool Status
host.description: Use this when you need to inspect whether windows host execution is enabled and which native programs are allowed.

host.name: windows_host_capture_display
host.title: Capture Windows Host Display
host.description: Compatibility alias for host_capture_display. On Windows this retains the original PR tool name.

quality.description: Requested image quality from 1 through 100. Native lossless PNG backends record but do not apply JPEG quality.

host.name: windows_host_capture_program
host.title: Capture Windows Host Window by PID
host.description: Compatibility alias for host_capture_window. On Windows this retains the original PR tool name.

pid.description: Host process ID whose visible application window should be captured.

include_process_tree.description: Also consider visible windows owned by child processes, useful for launchers, browsers, emulators, and multi-process GUI applications.

host.name: windows_host_exec
host.title: Run Windows PowerShell Command
host.description: Compatibility alias for host_exec. Use this when you explicitly need native windows host tooling rather than the Windows host devbox.

host.name: windows_host_inspect_file
host.title: Inspect Windows Host File Integrity
host.description: Use this when a Windows host command references a file that may be corrupted, mojibake-encoded, syntactically broken, or otherwise suspect on disk. It inspects exact bytes and PowerShell parser status where relevant.

host.name: windows_host_read_large_file
host.title: Read Large Windows Host File Chunk
host.description: Use this when you need an exact byte range from a Windows host file so you can diagnose or repair corruption without lossy UTF-8 conversion.

path.description: File path on the Windows host.

working_dir.description: Working directory used to resolve relative Windows host paths. Defaults to the configured host working directory.

offset_bytes.description: Starting byte offset within the file.

max_bytes.description: Maximum raw bytes to return from that offset.

host.name: windows_host_run_program
host.title: Run Allowed Windows Host Program
host.description: Compatibility alias for host_run_program. Use this when you need a specific allowed windows host program with structured arguments.

host.name: windows_host_status
host.title: Windows Host Tool Status
host.description: Compatibility alias for host_status. Use this when you need to inspect whether windows host execution is enabled and which native programs are allowed.

host.name: windows_host_write_large_file
host.title: Write Large Windows Host File
host.description: Use this when you need to create or overwrite a Windows host file using exact bytes, especially to repair corruption while preserving the intended payload end to end.

path.description: File path on the Windows host.

working_dir.description: Working directory used to resolve relative Windows host paths. Defaults to the configured host working directory.

content.description: Optional UTF-8 text payload to write. Provide either content or content_base64.

content_base64.description: Base64-encoded raw bytes to write exactly as provided. Provide either content or content_base64.

append.description: Append to the file instead of overwriting it.

create_dirs.description: Create parent directories if they do not exist.

expected_sha256.description: Optional expected SHA-256 of the decoded payload for end-to-end verification.
